summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found a compact US-listed universe around adult online universities, employer-affiliated degree pathways, workforce certificates, institutional payments, and career-training platforms. STRA is the clearest direct reference asset owner because its US higher-education segment includes Capella and Strayer, while its ETS segment explicitly manages employer education-benefit relationships. LRN and LINC provide adjacent workforce/career-learning exposure, with LINC more vocational and employer-partner oriented. NNI is the underfollowed supplier/platform candidate: not an online university, but its education technology and payments segment sits inside the institutional tuition-payment and education-services workflow. This Layer 1B pass expands the universe around scarce distribution, employer-connected training capacity, payments, education technology services, and completion infrastructure for adult online and workforce-linked education. The more underfollowed exposure appears less in famous university brands and more in companies that own employer relationships, accredited delivery capacity, regulated student-payment/servicing rails, or career-training pathways that can convert adult demand into enrollments and job mobility. Candidate list is capped at four and intentionally favors small/mid-cap or niche public companies over mega-cap education technology references.
